why: Choosing non-overlapping screenings to maximise total audience is weighted interval scheduling: sort shows by end time, and for each show binary search the last show that ends strictly before it starts, then dp[i] = max(skip, take). The week's binary search is the lookup inside the DP.
hints: Greedy by earliest end works only when every show is worth the same. Here volumes differ, so think about 'take it or skip it' for each show.

Sort shows by end = start + duration. dp[i] = best total using the first i shows; show i either is skipped (dp[i-1]) or taken (volume + dp[j], where j counts the shows ending strictly before its start).
Find j with bisect_left on the sorted end times. Sorting plus n binary searches: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
pitfalls: A show that ends at time t conflicts with one starting at t: use end < start (bisect_left), not end <= start.
The end time is start + duration, not start + duration - 1; example 2 only gives 4 with this convention.
Sort by end time, not start time, or the prefix dp is not valid.
statement:
A media company is showing exclusive content in theaters. There are n scheduled screenings. Screening i starts at start[i], lasts duration[i], and is expected to draw volume[i] viewers.

Pick a set of screenings with no two overlapping and return the largest possible total volume.

  • Screening i occupies the time from start[i] to end[i] = start[i] + duration[i].
  • Two screenings are compatible only if one fully concludes before the other begins: end[a] < start[b]. A screening ending at time 3 and another starting at time 3 overlap.

Worked example. start = [1, 2, 4], duration = [2, 2, 1], volume = [1, 2, 3].

  • Screening 0 runs 1 to 3, screening 1 runs 2 to 4, screening 2 runs 4 to 5.
  • Screenings 1 and 2 touch at time 4, so they overlap and cannot both be chosen (that would give 5).
  • Screening 0 ends at 3 < 4, so screenings 0 and 2 are compatible: 1 + 3 = 4.
  • No compatible set does better, so the answer is 4.

In the first published example the best choice is the screening starting at 5 (ends 17, volume 51) plus the one starting at 18 (volume 25), for 76.
